title: Tensor powers and duals of an invertible module after scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $M$ be a locally free $R$-module sheaf of rank one, meaning locally isomorphic to $R$ in the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use tensor products and powers of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every integer $r\geq0$ there is a canonical natural $S$-linear isomorphism
$$ (M^{\otimes_R r})\otimes_R S\simeq(M\otimes_R S)^{\otimes_S r}, $$
where the case $r=0$ is the tensor unitor. There is also a canonical natural isomorphism
$$M^\vee\otimes_R S\simeq(M\otimes_R S)^\vee$$
with $M^\vee=\mathcal{H}om_R(M,R)$ as in [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and these comparisons commute with the tensor-power associators, the unitors, and iteration of ring maps.

source.place: proof paragraph (3), tensor powers and dual evaluation under ordinary scalar extension

proof.text: Obtain normalized binary comparison data from [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence]. Construct the power comparison from the unit in degree zero, identity in degree one, and binary comparison followed by tensoring the preceding power comparison for r+2. Prove its naturality by two-step induction, using binary bifunctor naturality and naturality of the second-factor map.

Use the explicit dual isomorphisms and normalized scalar-extension towers of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-dual-tower-core]. Derive the power tower square by two-step induction: degree zero is its unit square, degree one uses scalar extension of identity, and the successor step moves the preceding power comparison through binary naturality, applies the induction hypothesis inside tensoring, and finishes with the binary tower square.

Assemble the constructed power comparisons and explicit dual and tower maps directly into InvertibleTensorScalarExtensionData of [def-sp-scalar-tensor-comparison-data], using the dual evaluation formula and contravariant naturality of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-dual-evaluation], invertibility of the scalar extension of M from [lem-sp-scalar-extension-dual-local-iso], and the dual tower theorem of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-dual-tower-core] for the corresponding fields. No intermediate comparison record is needed. The original theorem signature and all its fields are unchanged.
